questions: What is the exact definition of a "good string" in terms of its relationship to sequence A and the allowed operations?
How exactly does the operation "replace each of A_i and A_{i+1}" modify the sequence A - does it set both to 1, or toggle them, or follow some other rule?
Are the indices in the operations considered modulo N, and if so, how does this affect the boundary conditions when i=N-1 or i=N?
Can the same position in sequence A be modified multiple times through different operations, or is each position limited to being modified once?
What constitutes a valid "good string" - must it allow transforming A to all 1s, or just ensure no 0s remain after any sequence of operations?
Are there any constraints on the length or content of string S beyond having length N and consisting of characters that enable the operations?
How should overlapping or conflicting operations be handled when they could potentially modify the same elements of A?
Is the initial sequence A guaranteed to have at least one 0, or must the solution handle cases where A already contains no 0s?
answers: A string S makes A good if the operations can be applied (any number of times, possibly zero) until A contains no 0, as stated.
The operation sets both A_i and A_{i+1} to 1 (not toggle or any other rule).
Only as given by the stated wraparound definitions (S_{N+1}=S_1, etc.); not specified further.
Not specified beyond 'any number of times'; a position may be affected by multiple operations.
It must allow making A contain no 0s at all, as stated -- not merely avoid contradiction.
S has length N and consists only of uppercase English letters; no further restriction is given.
Not specified beyond what's given; operations may be applied in any order, including ones affecting overlapping positions.
Not guaranteed; A could already contain no 0s, in which case zero operations are needed.
inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N, consisting of 0 and 1. We call a string S of length N, a good string if it is possible to perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero) so that the sequence A contains no 0. Here, S_i (1\leq i\leq N) denotes the i-th character of S, and we define S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, and A_{N+1}=A_1. A string S makes A good if the operations can be applied (any number of times, possibly zero) until A contains no 0, as stated. - Perform one of the following operations: - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_i= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_{i+2}= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1}. - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_{i+2}= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_i= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. Determine whether there exists a good string. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there exists a good string, print Yes; otherwise, print No. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Yes, outputs such as yes, YES, or yEs will also be accepted. Constraints - 3\leq N\leq 200000 - A_i\in \lbrace 0,1 \rbrace (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
